lens: evidence integrity, privacy, and safe action

artifact.surface: versioned localhost HTTP API and deterministic local effect adapter
artifact.environment: isolated Docker Compose project with synthetic accounts only

dimensions.evidence: TS-ID-01 persisted no assertion or action; TS-ID-03 rejected candidate attribution from a recruiter-forwarded statement; cross-account reads returned scoped 404 responses.
Every assertion stored an exact contiguous evidence span and source item; deterministic replay, confirmation history, and conditional supersession were exercised.
Ambiguous identity, relative time, no_action, blocked inference, explicit temporal conflict, supersession, failed effects, and unknown outcomes had distinct tested states.
Approval before fact decisions failed; approvals were exact-preview and version bound; stale, revoked, expired-capability, and deleted-source execution paths were rejected at execution time.

The only adapter was labeled local simulation. Duplicate execution reused one attempt, failure supported reviewed retry, timeout blocked blind retry, and success required destination readback. No live integration or general write capability existed.

Purpose, account scope, immediate access revocation, content/hash redaction, orphan identity redaction, simulated-destination removal, and deletion lineage were directly tested. Automated retention expiry, export, backup erasure, and vendor lifecycle were outside this local slice.

The shared schema permits only candidate-momentum fields and prepare_question. A polished culture-fit/candidate-quality request was rejected and the OpenAPI contract exposed no calendar or generic connector capability.
The eight-case gold fixture, atomic failure checks, source-only unit discovery, direct HTTP walkthrough, service health evidence, and recovery checks were deterministic and inspectable.

findings.observation: The slice records retention intent and implements deletion propagation, but it has no expiry worker, user export, backup-erasure proof, or private-asset object-store lifecycle.
findings.user_impact: Promoting this local slice to real candidate data could retain or omit governed data beyond a user's expected lifecycle.
findings.recommendation: Keep the backend synthetic/local-only until retention execution, export, backup policy, and separate private-asset storage are implemented and tested end to end.
findings.verification: Run a dated lifecycle test that expires, exports, deletes, restores from backup, and verifies every registered derivative without exposing source content in logs.

findings.observation: Authentication intentionally uses seeded simulated humans and is refused when NODE_ENV is production.
findings.user_impact: The current session mechanism proves account scoping for local clients but is not evidence of production identity assurance, recovery, or administrative revocation.
findings.recommendation: Replace simulated login with a production identity provider and governed session administration before any non-synthetic deployment.
findings.verification: Exercise account invitation, role change, session revocation, stolen-token containment, and cross-account access with production-equivalent identities.

findings.observation: Reconciliation is proven for the deterministic local destination, while reversal semantics for real contact, calendar, ATS, CRM, or messaging systems are intentionally absent.
findings.user_impact: A future live connector could require correction or reversal behavior that this simulation does not establish.
findings.recommendation: Admit each connector separately with an exact effect contract, destination-specific readback, reconciliation, and reversible correction where the platform permits.
findings.verification: Use connector-specific duplicate, timeout-before, timeout-after, permission-revocation, mismatch, retry, and reversal cases before enabling a live write.

strengths: Observed evidence, proposal, user fact decision, confirmed temporal state, action proposal, approval, attempt, observation, outcome, audit, and deletion lineage remain separate persisted records.
The TS-CORE-01 walkthrough shows two clients sharing one account-scoped authority while a fixture compiler remains proposal-only.
Unknown and simulated outcomes are labeled truthfully; no destination readback means no verified success.
Candidate fit, quality, personality, protected-trait, and acceptance scoring are structurally outside the shared contract.
missing_evidence: Production identity-provider behavior and operational session controls
Real candidate-data retention, export, backup, restore, encryption, and regional controls
Private screenshot or asset storage and derived-store deletion
Live connector correctness, reversal, and provider reconciliation
OCR or model extraction quality and field recruiter value
open_questions: Which production identity provider and role model will own account membership?
What retention and export promises will be user-visible before real capture is admitted?
Which single live connector, if any, can prove destination readback and safe correction first?
